text: The De Gennes Prize, previously called the Prize for Materials Chemistry, was established in 2008 and is awarded biennially by the Royal Society of Chemistry for outstanding and exceptional contributions in the field of materials chemistry. The prize honors the legacy of Pierre-Gilles de Gennes. The recipient receives £5000, a medal, a certificate, and completes a UK lecture tour. Pierre-Gilles de Gennes was born in Paris, France, in 1932 and graduated from Ecole Normale in 1955. He then worked as a research engineer at the Atomic Energy Centre (Saclay) before spending a brief period at the University of California, Berkeley and 27 months in the French Navy. He later became an assistant professor at the University of Paris in Orsay, where he conducted research on superconductors and liquid crystals. In 1991, de Gennes was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his studies on the boundary lines between order and disorder in materials such as liquid crystals. Following the Nobel Prize, he visited approximately 200 high schools between 1992 and 1994, delivering talks on science, innovation, and common sense to students. Pierre-Gilles de Gennes passed away at the age of 74 on 18 May 2007.
